chapter_theme: The attainment of eight-limbed yoga (அட்டாங்கயோகப் பேறு): those who love Siva's feet and practise reach the Siva-state, where the gods come out to meet them, hail them as their lord or as Hara himself, and they dwell in bliss by the Lord's grace. The chapter ends by defining samadhi as joining the Supreme beyond all limiting adjuncts.
structure_note: Four verses (633 to 636) describe the welcome by the gods, framed by a verse of grace to the devotee (632) and closing with verses on who reaches what (637, 638) and a definition of samadhi (639).

632.reading: Those who delight in the feet of the matted-haired one who gladly rises into the flower will go to Amaravati; the one on the great bull, who dances with the lady, will grant grace, asking 'what did this one desire?'
632.nuance: போது உகந்து ஏறும் (who delights to mount the flower) is traditionally the Lord rising in the heart's lotus; Sengalvaraya parallels Kural 3. அமராபதி is Indra's heaven, a lower goal than release, which the next verses go beyond. ஏதுகந்தான் இவன் may be 'what does he want?', a gracious question, as read here.

633.reading: For those who hold to his feet with love, learn the Supreme's praise and contemplate him where they are, sages come to meet them as they rise, and they can reach the clear Siva-state.
633.nuance: The means named here are devotional (love, learning his praise, contemplation), though the chapter is the fruit of yoga. முற்றெழுந்தாங்கே may be 'as they rise in full' or 'as they rise at the end'.

634.reading: Having worshipped and done austerity and become king of the gods, they are hailed as the lord of Amaravati, and with cool drums and flutes sounding they dwell in bliss: this is the Lord's grace.
634.nuance: Whether the yogi literally becomes Indra or is welcomed like a king of the gods is open. The last words credit the bliss to grace, not to the austerity.

635.reading: At the time they go and reach the red-gold Siva-way, hosts of gods come out to meet them, saying 'this is our golden lord', and they may dwell in blissful union.
635.nuance: கும்பத்து அமரர் is unclear: the gods of the dome of heaven, or of the summit in the body. இன்பக் கலவி (blissful union) is union with Siva. The gods now call the yogi their lord, a step beyond 634.

636.reading: When he arrives, the gods of the directions ask 'who is this?', are told 'this is Hara', and all the splendid gods come to meet him: so he truly saw the dark-throated one.
636.nuance: The yogi is taken for Siva himself, which the verse gives as the proof that he truly saw Siva. மெய்கண்ட (truly saw) may also echo the name of the Siddhanta's Meykandar, but nothing in the verse requires it.

637.reading: Those of the true word who seek the good way and turn aside Death's way, and householders whose great giving never shrinks, though they reach the gods' many ways in the eight directions, find it becomes the way of the earth.
637.nuance: பார்வழி யாகுமே is the crux. Read as 'it leads back to the earth', the verse says merit wins heavens but not release, against the yogi's attainment. Read as 'it becomes the way for the world', it praises such people as a model. Both stand.

638.reading: For those able to rest in absorption, and those able to draw in the seven worlds, it stands as strength; for those able to store it, it is nectar to revel in; for those able to bear it, it becomes their own dwelling.
638.nuance: The subject is not stated; it may be the Lord, the attainment or the yogic power. Each line names a capacity (வல்லார்க்கு, those able to) and a matching gift. The variants alter case endings but not the sense.

639.reading: Going beyond the limiting adjunct that is effect, so that the seven noble causes come to oneself, and in the austerity that is the noble cause joining the Supreme: that is samadhi.
639.nuance: உபாதி (upadhi, limiting adjunct) and காரியம், காரணம் (effect, cause) are technical; the seven causes are not identified in the verse. தாரியல் may be 'garlanded' or a form of 'bearing'. The definition parallels 597's for dharana and 628's for samadhi.

links.note: Both speak of the one who goes upon the flower and of those who reach his feet. The Kural promises they live long upon the earth (or, as Parimelazhagar takes it, in the world of release); Tirumular promises Amaravati, then in the following verses the Siva-state.

597 defines dharana as holding with the Supreme (தரித்தது தாரணை தற்பரத்தோடே) after dissolving body into elements and mind; 639 defines samadhi as joining the Supreme (தற்பரஞ் சேர்தல்) after going beyond all upadhi. The two limbs differ as holding and joining.
585 makes pratyahara the separating and dissolving of upadhi from the inner light; 639 makes samadhi the going beyond upadhi altogether, so the two verses mark stages on one line.

source_issues: 635: கும்பத் தமரர் is unclear and may be corrupt.
639: the seven causes (காரணம் ஏழும்) are unexplained and தாரியல் is unclear.
